newsitem.title: FRANCE: French reforms must continue - Chirac.
newsitem.headline: French reforms must continue - Chirac.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac told his cabinet on Wednesday that reforms necessary to modernise France must go ahead "come what may", government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said.
"We must make sure that people believe that we will continue, come what may, the reforms necessary for our country," Lamassoure quoted him as telling the weekly cabinet meeting.

The centre-right government faces trade union hostility to two key pieces of legislation due being debated by parliament this month -- the reform of the SNCF state railways and the creating of private pension funds.

Facing tense relations with organised labour over record 12.7 percent unemployment, stagnant growth and controversial moves towards privatisation and competition in public services, Chirac sought to emphasise moves to make the French state more user-friendly.

"We will modernise the relationship between the state and citizens, and every ministry must be involved in this effort," Chirac said. "We must make this better known to the French people. Ministers must not hesitate to present popular reforms."

The cabinet adopted a decree on decentralising administrative decisions concerning private citizens and heard a report from ministers on simplifying procedures for receiving identity documents and on hospital reform.
Chirac said France had taken a first major step towards decentralisation more than a decade ago but reform of the state had since got bogged down.
"In the last year, we have started to move from words to action," he added.
